name: The New York EDITION
positioning: Design hotel by Ian Schrager in a 1909 clocktower building on Madison Avenue, steps from Madison Square Park
best_for: Travelers who want a design-led base in the Flatiron area
Guests who enjoy hotel bars and a British-style restaurant

facts.text: The building was originally constructed in 1909 as the Metropolitan Life Insurance Company Headquarters.
The hotel was designed by Ian Schrager.
The hotel is steps from Madison Square Park.
The clocktower has 360-degree views of New York City.
Guest rooms and suites have oak floors and dark oak wood-paneled foyers.
Room views range from Madison Square Park to the Empire State Building to the New York City skyline.
The Clocktower restaurant serves contemporary British cuisine.
The Lobby Bar serves bespoke seasonal cocktails and light bites.
Room service offers all-day dining options, including breakfast in bed.

highlights.text: The Bar at The Clocktower has a 24k gold leaf bar, a fiberglass globe chandelier and carved plaster ceilings.
The Clocktower restaurant has three dining rooms overlooking Madison Square Park and the Flatiron District.
The spa is on the 39th floor.
Hotel suites display large black and white photography from Melvin Sokolsky's 1963 Bubble series.
The gym has four Peloton bicycles and 24 hour access.

considerations.text: Valet car retrieval can take 1.5 hours at peak arrival and departure times.
A private car from JFK takes approximately one hour.
WhataHotel notes the modern minimalist design may feel stark to some guests.
